<!--
TODO: revisit once more core faculty data is available. These choices are
tailored to the current small number of core faculty (7 people, 4 with
evaluations before the program) and a single program start date.

Program start / definitions
- `core_start` is hard-coded to 2025-01-01 for everyone. `evaluator.core_faculty_start`
  holds a per-person start date; if starts become staggered, define
  before/after per person (and the vertical line on the charts no longer applies)
- "Ever-core" lumps anyone who was core at some point. If faculty leave the
  program, their later non-core evaluations currently count as "Ever-core / After"
- Periods are based on rotation date, not on when the evaluation was written

Charts
- `person_colors` only has 8 palette slots: with more than 8 ever-core faculty
  the per-person stacked bar and line charts get NA colours. Switch to
  small multiples (facet per person) or fold into "Other"
- `clerkship_colors` is hard-coded to Medicine/Neurology; new clerkships with
  core faculty get no colour
- `date_breaks = "1 month"` on all x-axes will get crowded over a longer period
- The x-axis range (`month_range`) is shared by all charts; core-only charts are
  empty before 2025
- Months with very few evaluations (e.g. a single one in July 2025) make the
  monthly averages noisy; consider a minimum n per month on the line charts

Statistics
- The "Very low n" warning callout and its wording assume very few core
  faculty; revise or remove once n is reasonable
- The caveat that both groups looked "roughly flat before 2025" is a
  statement about the current data; recheck, ideally with a formal pre-trend
  test (group × time interaction in the before period)
- The DiD model only has a random intercept per evaluator. With more core
  faculty add a random slope for period, `(1 + period | evaluator)`; the current
  df/p-value treat evaluations as fairly independent evidence of change
- Not adjusted for clerkship or academic title; add as covariates when the
  groups are large enough
- With more time points, consider an event-study / interrupted time series
  instead of a single before/after split

## Number of clerkship evaluations over time
Number of **formative** evaluations per month (by rotation date), core vs non-core faculty
```{r}
db <- ifelse(interactive(), "local/narrate.db", "../local/narrate.db")

last_modified <- format(file.info(db)$mtime, "%B %-d, %Y")

conn <- dbGetConn(db)

formative_evals <- tbl(conn, "evaluation") |>
  filter(summary_flg == 0) |>
  inner_join(
    tbl(conn, "rotation") |>
      select(rotation_id = id, rotation_date, clerkship_id),
    by = "rotation_id"
  ) |>
  inner_join(
    tbl(conn, "clerkship") |> select(clerkship_id = id, clerkship),
    by = "clerkship_id"
  ) |>
  select(
    evaluation_id = id,
    evaluator_id,
    core_faculty,
    rotation_date,
    clerkship
  ) |>
  collect() |>
  mutate(
    rotation_date = ymd(rotation_date),
    month = floor_date(rotation_date, unit = "month"),
    faculty = factor(
      if_else(core_faculty %in% 1, "Core", "Non-core"),
      levels = c("Non-core", "Core")
    ),
    clerkship = tools::toTitleCase(tolower(clerkship))
  )

formative_by_month <- formative_evals |> count(month, faculty)

faculty_colors <- c("Core" = "#2a78d6", "Non-core" = "#eb6834")
month_range <- range(formative_by_month$month) + c(-15, 15)

plot_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(colour = "grey90", linewidth = 0.3),
    axis.text = element_text(colour = "grey35"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.justification = "left",
    plot.title.position = "plot"
  )

# Start of the core faculty program, marked on the line charts
core_start <- as.Date("2025-01-01")
core_start_line <- list(
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = core_start,
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 0.4,
    colour = "grey50"
  ),
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = core_start,
    y = 100,
    label = "Core faculty program starts",
    hjust = -0.05,
    vjust = 1,
    size = 3.2,
    colour = "grey35"
  )
)

month_totals <- formative_by_month |> count(month, wt = n)

ggplot(formative_by_month, aes(month, n)) +
  geom_col(
    aes(fill = faculty),
    width = 25,
    colour = "white",
    linewidth = 0.4
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = month_totals,
    aes(label = n),
    vjust = -0.4,
    size = 3.5,
    colour = "grey20"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = faculty_colors, breaks = c("Core", "Non-core")) +
  scale_x_date(
    date_breaks = "1 month",
    date_labels = "%b %Y",
    limits = month_range,
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))) +
  labs(
    title = "Formative evaluations per month",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Evaluations",
    fill = NULL
  ) +
  plot_theme
```


```{r}
# Anyone who was core faculty at some point; evaluator rows sharing an
# original_evaluator_id (e.g. after a title change) are the same person
core_people <- tbl(conn, "evaluator") |>
  select(evaluator_id = id, original_evaluator_id, evaluator) |>
  collect() |>
  group_by(original_evaluator_id) |>
  filter(
    any(evaluator_id %in% formative_evals$evaluator_id[
      formative_evals$faculty == "Core"
    ])
  ) |>
  mutate(
    # Capitalise after spaces, apostrophes and hyphens (e.g. O'Hare)
    person = gsub(
      "(^|[ '-])([a-z])", "\\1\\U\\2",
      tolower(first(evaluator)),
      perl = TRUE
    )
  ) |>
  ungroup()

#  tbl(conn, "evaluator") |> collect() |> group_by(original_evaluator_id) |> filter(any(!is.na(core_faculty_start))) |> 
#   summarise(core_faculty_start = min(core_faculty_start, na.rm = T), person = gsub(
#       "(^|[ '-])([a-z])", "\\1\\U\\2",
#       tolower(min(evaluator, na.rm = T)),
#       perl = TRUE
#     ), .groups = "drop")

person_by_month <- formative_evals |>
  inner_join(core_people, by = "evaluator_id") |>
  count(month, person, faculty)

# Fixed palette order, assigned to people by total evaluations (most first)
person_order <- person_by_month |>
  count(person, wt = n, sort = TRUE) |>
  pull(person)
person_colors <- setNames(
  c(
    "#2a78d6", "#eb6834", "#1baf7a", "#eda100",
    "#e87ba4", "#008300", "#6250d6", "#e34948"
  )[seq_along(person_order)],
  person_order
)
person_by_month <- person_by_month |>
  mutate(person = factor(person, levels = person_order))
person_totals <- person_by_month |> count(month, wt = n)

ggplot(person_by_month, aes(month, n)) +
  geom_col(
    aes(fill = person, alpha = faculty),
    width = 25, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.4
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = person_totals, aes(label = n),
    vjust = -0.4, size = 3.5, colour = "grey20"
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = person_colors) +
  # Lighter shade for evaluations given before becoming core faculty
  scale_alpha_manual(
    values = c("Core" = 1, "Non-core" = 0.35),
    labels = c("Core" = "As core faculty", "Non-core" = "Before becoming core"),
    breaks = c("Core", "Non-core")
  ) +
  guides(
    fill = guide_legend(order = 1),
    alpha = guide_legend(order = 2, override.aes = list(fill = "grey30"))
  ) +
  scale_x_date(
    date_breaks = "1 month", date_labels = "%b %Y",
    limits = month_range, expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.12))) +
  labs(
    title = "Formative evaluations per month – faculty who were ever core",
    subtitle = "Includes their evaluations from before they became core faculty",
    x = NULL, y = "Evaluations", fill = NULL, alpha = NULL
  ) +
  plot_theme
```

# AI review scores over time
```{r}
# AI reviews (rubric `rubric_id`) of the formative evaluations of faculty who
# were ever core; review_scores() drops reviews that aren't completed
ai_reviews <- tbl(conn, "review_assignment") |>
  filter(rubric_id == local(rubric_id)) |>
  inner_join(
    tbl(conn, "reviewer") |> filter(human == 0) |> select(reviewer_id = id),
    by = "reviewer_id"
  ) |>
  select(review_id = id, evaluation_id) |>
  collect()

person_evals <- formative_evals |>
  inner_join(core_people, by = "evaluator_id") |>
  select(evaluation_id, month, person, faculty)

ai_quality <- ai_reviews |>
  inner_join(
    review_scores(conn, ai_reviews$review_id, error_on_incomplete = FALSE) |>
      transmute(review_id, quality = 100 * (coverage + avg_specificity + utility)),
    by = "review_id"
  )

person_scores <- ai_quality |>
  inner_join(person_evals, by = "evaluation_id") |>
  group_by(month, person, faculty) |>
  summarise(quality = mean(quality), n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(person = factor(person, levels = person_order))

ggplot(person_scores, aes(month, quality, colour = person)) +
  core_start_line +
  geom_line(aes(group = person), linewidth = 0.7) +
  # Hollow points for months before the person became core faculty
  geom_point(aes(shape = faculty), size = 2.5, stroke = 1, fill = "white") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = person_colors) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    values = c("Core" = 16, "Non-core" = 21),
    labels = c("Core" = "As core faculty", "Non-core" = "Before becoming core"),
    breaks = c("Core", "Non-core")
  ) +
  guides(
    colour = guide_legend(order = 1),
    shape = guide_legend(order = 2, override.aes = list(colour = "grey30"))
  ) +
  scale_x_date(
    date_breaks = "1 month", date_labels = "%b %Y",
    limits = month_range, expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
  labs(
    title = "Average AI quality score per month – faculty who were ever core",
    subtitle = glue(
      "Rubric {rubric_id}; months with few evaluations are noisy"
    ),
    x = NULL, y = "Mean quality score (0–100)", colour = NULL, shape = NULL
  ) +
  plot_theme
```

```{r}
# Monthly average for the ever-core group combined (incl. before they became
# core) vs all other faculty
group_scores <- ai_quality |>
  inner_join(
    formative_evals |> select(evaluation_id, evaluator_id, month),
    by = "evaluation_id"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    group = if_else(
      evaluator_id %in% core_people$evaluator_id,
      "Ever-core faculty", "All other faculty"
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(month, group) |>
  summarise(quality = mean(quality), n = n(), .groups = "drop")

group_colors <- c("Ever-core faculty" = "#2a78d6", "All other faculty" = "#eb6834")

ggplot(group_scores, aes(month, quality, colour = group)) +
  core_start_line +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = group_colors) +
  scale_x_date(
    date_breaks = "1 month", date_labels = "%b %Y",
    limits = month_range, expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 100), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.02))) +
  labs(
    title = "Average AI quality score per month – ever-core vs all other faculty",
    subtitle = glue("Rubric {rubric_id}; formative evaluations only"),
    x = NULL, y = "Mean quality score (0–100)", colour = NULL
  ) +

HTML(glue("Data last modified {last_modified}"))
```

# Impact of the core faculty program

The question is whether the quality of formative evaluations written by core
faculty, as scored by the AI review (rubric `r rubric_id`), changed after the
core faculty program started on January 1, 2025. A simple before/after
comparison is not enough: the ever-core faculty already scored higher before the
program, and scores for everyone may shift over time for unrelated reasons. Both
analyses below therefore compare the **change** in scores of the ever-core
faculty with the change in scores of all other faculty over the same period
(evaluations are assigned to a period by rotation date).

```{r}
did_data <- ai_quality |>
  inner_join(
    formative_evals |> select(evaluation_id, evaluator_id, month),
    by = "evaluation_id"
  ) |>
  inner_join(
    tbl(conn, "evaluator") |>
      select(evaluator_id = id, original_evaluator_id) |>
      collect(),
    by = "evaluator_id"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    group = factor(
      if_else(evaluator_id %in% core_people$evaluator_id, "Ever-core", "Other"),
      levels = c("Other", "Ever-core")
    ),
    period = factor(
      if_else(month >= core_start, "After", "Before"),
      levels = c("Before", "After")
    )
  )

did_data |>
  group_by(group, period) |>
  summarise(
    Faculty = n_distinct(original_evaluator_id),
    Evaluations = n(),
    `Mean score` = round(mean(quality), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  rename(Group = group, Period = period) |>
  kable(caption = "AI quality score (0–100) by group and period")

# Ever-core faculty with evaluations both before and after the program start
n_core_both <- did_data |>
  filter(group == "Ever-core") |>
  group_by(original_evaluator_id) |>
  filter(n_distinct(period) == 2) |>
  pull(original_evaluator_id) |>
  n_distinct()
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Very low n: interpret with caution
Only `r n_core_both` ever-core faculty members have evaluations **both before and
after** the program started, so the change in the ever-core group rests on very
few people and the statistical power of these tests is very low. With so little
data a non-significant result says little about whether the program had an
effect, and a significant result is likely to overestimate the size of the
effect and can be driven by a single person. Treat the results below as
exploratory.
:::

## Difference-in-differences model

A linear mixed model of the AI quality score of each evaluation:

`quality ~ group * period + (1 | evaluator)`

- `group`: ever-core vs other faculty; captures the difference in level
  between the groups before the program
- `period`: before vs after January 1, 2025; captures the change over time
  that applies to all faculty
- `group × period` (the **difference-in-differences**): the additional change
  in score for the ever-core faculty on top of the change seen for everyone
  else. This is the estimate of the program's effect, in quality score points
- `(1 | evaluator)`: a random intercept per faculty member, so that faculty with
  many evaluations don't count as many independent observations and each person
  is compared against their own typical score. This also accounts for the fact 
  that some faculty members systematically give higher scores than others.

The model is fitted by REML with `lmerTest`, which gives p-values for each term
using Satterthwaite's approximation of the degrees of freedom; confidence
intervals are 95% Wald intervals.

```{r}
did_model <- lmerTest::lmer(
  quality ~ group * period + (1 | original_evaluator_id),
  data = did_data
)
did_coef <- summary(did_model)$coefficients
did_ci <- confint(did_model, method = "Wald")[rownames(did_coef), ]

data.frame(
  Term = c(
    "Intercept (other faculty, before)",
    "Ever-core vs other (before)",
    "After vs before (other faculty)",
    "Difference-in-differences (ever-core × after)"
  ),
  Estimate = round(did_coef[, "Estimate"], 1),
  `CI low` = round(did_ci[, 1], 1),
  `CI high` = round(did_ci[, 2], 1),
  df = round(did_coef[, "df"]),
  p = format.pval(did_coef[, "Pr(>|t|)"], digits = 2, eps = 0.001),
  check.names = FALSE
) |>
  kable(row.names = FALSE, caption = "Fixed effects (score points)")

did_term <- "groupEver-core:periodAfter"
did_est <- did_coef[did_term, "Estimate"]
did_est_ci <- did_ci[did_term, ]
did_p <- did_coef[did_term, "Pr(>|t|)"]
```

After the program started, the scores of ever-core faculty changed by
**`r sprintf("%+.1f", did_est)` points** (95% CI
`r sprintf("%.1f", did_est_ci[1])` to `r sprintf("%.1f", did_est_ci[2])`)
relative to the change for all other faculty
(p = `r format.pval(did_p, digits = 2, eps = 0.001)`).

## Per-faculty change (Wilcoxon rank-sum test)

A simpler check that makes no assumptions about the distribution of the scores.
For each faculty member with evaluations both before and after January 1,
2025, the change is their mean score after minus their mean score before. The
changes of the ever-core faculty are then compared with those of all other
faculty using a Wilcoxon rank-sum test, with each person counting once. The
location shift is the Hodges-Lehmann estimate of the difference in change
between the groups. Ever-core faculty without evaluations before the program
can't contribute to this test.

```{r}
person_change <- did_data |>
  group_by(original_evaluator_id, group) |>
  summarise(
    before = mean(quality[period == "Before"]),
    after = mean(quality[period == "After"]),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(before), !is.na(after)) |>
  mutate(change = after - before)

person_change |>
  group_by(Group = group) |>
  summarise(
    Faculty = n(),
    `Median before` = median(before),
    `Median after` = median(after),
    `Median change` = median(change)
  ) |>
  kable(digits = 1, caption = "Per-faculty mean AI quality score (0–100)")

# group levels are Other, Ever-core, so the shift is Other - Ever-core; flip it
wilcox_res <- wilcox.test(change ~ group, data = person_change, conf.int = TRUE)
wilcox_shift <- -wilcox_res$estimate[[1]]
wilcox_ci <- -rev(wilcox_res$conf.int)
```

The change in score for ever-core faculty differed from that of other faculty
by **`r sprintf("%+.1f", wilcox_shift)` points** (95% CI
`r sprintf("%.1f", wilcox_ci[1])` to `r sprintf("%.1f", wilcox_ci[2])`;
Wilcoxon rank-sum p = `r format.pval(wilcox_res$p.value, digits = 2, eps = 0.001)`),
based on `r sum(person_change$group == "Ever-core")` ever-core and
`r sum(person_change$group == "Other")` other faculty.

## Caveats

- Ever-core faculty without evaluations before the program only add to the
  group level, not to the estimated change
- Core faculty were likely selected for being good evaluators, so the groups
  are not comparable by design. The difference-in-differences accounts for
  their higher starting level, but assumes both groups would have followed the
  same trend without the program (the monthly chart above suggests both were
  roughly flat before 2025)
- Other differences between the groups (e.g. clerkship, academic title) are not
  adjusted for
- The outcome is the AI review score, so conclusions depend on how well it
  agrees with human reviewers (see the AI–human concordance analysis)
